steps.action: Ensure that the sound volume is turned to a reasonable level and that the sound is not muted by clicking on the Volume Control applet (the speaker icon in the notification area) and setting the volume
On the Unity panel, select Home Folder
Open the Examples folder. Open the Ubuntu_Free_Culture_Showcase folder
Select either of the .ogg files
verifications: The file opens in your default media player
Sound is played through the speakers without noises or distortions.

steps.action: Adjust the volume with the Volume Control applet. Verify that the audio volume changes.
Right-click the Volume Control applet and check Mute
verifications: The audio mutes.

steps.action: Right-click the Volume Control applet and uncheck Mute
verifications: The audio resumes

steps.action: Boot up the image
verifications: FAMILY boot screen is displayed

steps.action: When ubiquity starts select your language in the left column
verifications: Language is selected, all labels are changed to translated versions

steps.action: Press "Try FAMILY" and wait for the Live session to start
verifications: The default desktop is displayed

steps.action: Connect the microphone to the computer.  (This can include a microphone on a headset)
Right click on the '''Volume Control''' icon on the right side of the top panel
Open ''Sound Preferences'' or ''Sound Setting''.
Go to the ''Input'' tab and ensure that the ''Input'' volume of the microphone is set to an appropriate level and is not muted.
Press the ''Super Windows key'', or click the Ubuntu logo in the upper left hand unity panel and search '''Sound Recorder'''.
Click the ''Record'' button (the red circle).
Talk briefly into the microphone.
Click the ''Stop'' button (the gray square).
Click the ''Play'' button (the right-facing triangle).
verifications: Your voice is played back and and no words have been dropped. (Remember to reset your microphone volume to prevent feedback on the internal microphone.)

steps.action: Ensure that Network Manager is running and that no networks are currently connected
Open Terminal
Ensure wireless is enabled
After approximately 30 seconds, open the network manager
verifications: Your wireless network is visible

steps.action: Connect to your wireless network
Run ifconfig in the terminal
verifications: A new network interface (e.g. "wlan0") is present and has received an IP address

steps.action: Run route -n . Note the IP address in the Gateway column. (not "0.0.0.0")
Run ping -c 5 [gateway] where [gateway] is the IP address of the Gateway, above.
verifications: The command reports "5 packets transmitted, 5 packets received"

steps.action: Insert a media card into the reader
verifications: The card is recognised

steps.action: Open the file manager
Find the media card in the menu on the left. Right click on this and open it
verifications: A window opens showing the contents of the card (if any)

steps.action: Right-click within the window and select Create Document → Create Empty File. Call the file test.txt
verifications: test.txt is created

steps.action: Drag test.txt to the trash can in the left hand menu
verifications: test.txt is removed from the card

steps.action: Close the card window
Eject the card
verifications: The icon is removed from the desktop

steps.action: Repeat for every type of media supported (e.g. CF, SD, MMC, etc.)
If you installed Xubuntu using English as the default keyboard layout and language, try to add different languages for your system:
Go to Language Support (Applications -> Settings Manager -> Language Support)
Press the Install / Remove Languages...
Select as many languages as you like, and install them by pressing the Apply Changes button
When they have been successfully installed, log out from the session, and select alternating languages at the login screen, next to the right of the session selector (Xubuntu Session)
verifications: Confirm that the main menus and outputs in the desktop are translated

steps.action: Tap super to show the dash
Click on the file lens icon
Make a search
verifications: It should impact the result on each category

steps.action: Open the filter by clicking on "Filter Results"
Change the filters for each of filter type
verifications: It should change the results, at least on one category

steps.action: Open any application and suspend machine
verifications: Machine suspends

steps.action: Restart suspended machine and unlock
verifications: Desktop shows previously started application

steps.action: 'ssh-keyscan -t rsa, dsa $hostname': should differ for each running instance.
You can ssh to instance as 'ubuntu@${hostname}'
Ubuntu user can 'sudo' without password prompt, and that 'sudo -l' contains '(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL'.
Attempt to ssh to each running instance as 'root@${hostname}'.
verifications: Access is denied and provides a message suggesting use of 'ubuntu' user.

steps.action: Run 'apt-get update' and verify that an ec2 mirror is used.
verifications: ec2 mirror looks like '(region).archive.ubuntu.com'.

steps.action: Running 'ec2-get-console-output' returns console output with boot messages
Install the core task in a current release.
Obtain all updates for your system.
Make sure xubuntu-desktop is not installed.
Upgrade to the development release.
verifications: This should upgrade without installing any metapackages.

steps.action: Go though the Ubiquity install as you would any other install. Most options won't matter for this testcase, but be sure to choose the following options
verifications: - Do NOT name the user mythtv. - Automatic (Guided) Partitioning. - "Frontend". - If you have no remote, choose no remote suppport. - For the security key, enter the PIN from the backend (in the backend testcase, this is set to 1234)

steps.action: Once installation is finished, remove the installation media and reboot.
Once the machine boots up, it should boot into the frontend.
Select "Watch TV". (this will only work if you have a backend already in the network)
verifications: The demo video should start playing.

steps.action: Install the specific release you wish to dist-upgrade from
Install all updates available for the release you want to upgrade by running update-manager. Click Check if any update is availabe, and click Install to install them
Watch it update, noting any errors
Reboot into your new system:
verifications: Any errors encountered during the upgrade? Any errors encountered after rebooting to new desktop? Does your hardware still work properly? Are you experiencing any application or background service crashes?

steps.action: Open a Word document format .doc or .docx and save it in ODF format.
verifications: The file can be opened and saved correctly in the revised format.

steps.action: Then open the document again.
verifications: After the closing and opening, do the contents look the same in the different file formats?

steps.action: Please ensure the Nautilus window is running and the Nautilus window is focused
Click the Search Icon in the top
Input 'test'
verifications: the 'test' folder was shown?

steps.action: Please ensure the Nautilus window is running and the Nautilus window is focused
Drag moveme.txt and drop into the folder test.
verifications: Is the file moveme.txt now located in 'test' folder?
